correctness.rationale: The exact model is specified with positive parameters and mode-reset convention. Published first-passage transforms are converted with p=1/tau_D and q=1/tau_v; the reset renewal map is strictly decreasing in the no-reset success transform. The symbolic identities P(h)=-pq(r+q)/(Dv²)<0 and P(K)=qr(r+q)(v²-D(r+q))/(Dv⁴) show distinct real positive exponents and classify the sign of the two-exponential difference. A strictly increasing exponential ratio gives exactly one crossing iff v²>D(q+r); otherwise no crossing. At the low-rate endpoint c_- has order sqrt(r) and at the critical endpoint order (r_c-r), yielding the asserted logarithmic ratios; continuity proves reentrant preference. The included SymPy program checked identities, representative sign orderings and endpoint limits. No finite experiment is used as the proof.

value.rationale: Which initial motion mode should be selected to minimize target-detection time is a physically motivated decision question in intermittent search. The theorem gives an exact sharp speed/reset boundary independent of one switching rate, proves that at most one target distance switches the better initial mode, and identifies logarithmically diverging distance scales at both ends of an advantageous reset-rate window. This is a global mechanism/phase diagram rather than an arbitrary numerical cut or routine derivative; the reentrant rate preference is a qualitative new use of the closed-form first-passage solution.
